ἄτιμος.kj: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)
ἄτιμος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5092 (τιμή);
ἄτιμος.as:
ἄτιμος, -ον
(< τιμή), [in LXX: Is 3:5 (קלה ni.), Is 53:3 (בּזה), Jb 30:4, 8 (בְּלִי־שֵׁם), Wi5, Si1*;]
without honour, dishonoured, despised: Mt 13:57, Mk 6:4, I Co 4:10; comp., I Co 12:23.†

ἀτιμάζω.long: I disgrace, treat disgracefully, dishonor, insult; I despise.
ἀτιμάζω.sd: to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat
ἀτιμάζω.kj: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully
ἀτιμάζω.as:
ἀτιμάζω
(< ἄτιμος), [in LXX for בּוּז, קלה, etc.;]
to dishonour, insult: Mk 12:4, TTr., mg., WH, Lk 20:11, Jo 8:49, Ro 2:23, Ja 2:6; pass.: Ac 5:41, Ro 1:24 (cf ἀτιμάω).†

ἀτενίζω.g: I direct my gaze, look steadily
ἀτενίζω.long: I direct my gaze, look steadily.
ἀτενίζω.kj: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes
ἀτενίζω.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (to stretch);
ἀτενίζω.as:
** ἀτενίζω
(< ἀτενής, strained, intent; < τείνω), [in LXX: I Es 6:28, III Mac 2:26*;]
to look fixedly, gaze (MM, s.v.): c. dat. pers., gaze upon: Lk 4:2022:56, Ac 3:1210:414:923:1; seq. εἰς, c. acc. pers., Ac 3:46:1513:9; metaph., Ac 1:107:5511:6, II Co 3:7, 13.†

ἄτεκνος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5043 (τέκνον);
ἄτεκνος.as:
ἄτεκνος, -ον
(< τέκνον), [in LXX: Ge 15:2, Le 20:20, 21 (עֲרִירִי), Is 49:21, Je 18:21 (שׁכל), Si 16:3*;]
childless: Lk 20:28, 29.†

ἄτερ.sd: aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively)
ἄτερ.der: a particle probably akin to G427 (ἄνευ);
ἄτερ.as:
** ἄτερ,
prep.,
[in LXX: II Mac 12:15*;]
in cl. most freq. in poets; without, apart from: c. gen., Lk 22:6, 35 (for exx. from π., v. MM, s.v.).†

ἄτοπος.long: (lit: out of place, unusual, unbecoming), improper, unrighteous, perverse.
ἄτοπος.sd: out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked
ἄτοπος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5117 (τόπος);
ἄτοπος.as:
ἄ-τοπος, -ον
(< τόπος), [in LXX: Jb 4:811:11, Pr 30:20 (24:55), al., for אָוֶן, etc.;]
1.out of place, not befitting.
2.marvellous, strange (of symptoms, Hipp.): Ac 28:6; hence, in late Greek, with ethical sense,
3.improper, unrighteous (so in LXX, and for exx. from π., v. M, II Th., 3:2; MM, s.v.): Lk 23:41, Ac 25:5, II Th 3:2.†

ἀτμίς.as:
ἀτμίς, -ίδος, ἡ,
[in LXX for עָנָן, תִּימָרָה, etc.;]
vapour: Ja 4:14; ἀ. καπνοῦ, Ac 2:19(LXX).†

Ἀττάλεια.long: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.
Ἀττάλεια.as:
Ἀτταλία (Rec. -άλεια), -υς, ἡ,
Attalia, a city of Pamphylia: Ac 14:25.†

ἀτιμία.as:
ἀτιμία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄτιμος), [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן, etc.;]
dishonour, disgrace: I Co 11:14, II Co 6:8; εἰς ἀ., Ro 9:21, II Ti 2:20; ἐν ἀ., I Co 15:43; κατ᾽ ἀ., II Co 11:21; πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions, Ro 1:26.†

ἄτομος.g: an indivisible part of time, a moment
ἄτομος.long: (lit: that cannot be cut), an indivisible part of time, a moment.
ἄτομος.sd: uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time)
ἄτομος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);
ἄτομος.as:
** ἄ-τομος, -ον
(< τέμνω), [in Sm.: Is 54:8 (MM, s.v.)*;]
indivisible; of time, ἄτομον, a moment: ἐν ἄ., I Co 15:52.†

ἄτακτος.long: (lit: out of order), disorderly, slack (in performance of duty).
ἄτακτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021 (τάσσω);
ἄτακτος.as:
** ἄ-τακτος, -ον
(< τάσσω), [in LXX: III Mac 1:19*;]
out of order, out of place (Lat. inordinatus), freq. of soldiers not keeping the ranks, or an army in disarray (cf. III Mac 1:19); hence, metaph., irregular, disorderly (v. previous word): I Th 5:14.†

ἀτάκτως.as:
** ἀ-τάκτως,
adv.,
[in Sm.: IV Ki 9:20*;]
disorderly, irregularly: II Th 3:6, 11.†

ἀτακτέω.long: (lit: I march out of order; then: I riot, rebel), behave disorderly, neglect my duty, am careless (or idle) in habits.
ἀτακτέω.as:
* ἀτακτέω, -ῶ
(< ἄτακτος),
primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaph., to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): II Th 3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, v. M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).†
